Q: Python TwitchIO Not connecting to channel. _websockets variable is an empty Dict A:

Option 1: Downgrade to TwitchIO 2.x

Don't pass client_secret :

It can use the Client Credentials flow to generate an App Token, overriding/ignoring the user token you're passing in.

super().__init__(
            token=token, # Your User OAuth token
            client_id=client_id,
            client_secret=client_secret, # <--- Drop this line
            bot_id=bot_id,
            owner_id=bot_id,
            prefix='!',
            initial_channels=self.initial_channels,
            nick=nick
        )

Option 2: Migrate Code for TwitchIO 3.x

Restructure to use add_token() to register user tokeans, and subscribe to EventSub events like ChatMessageSubscription . This should look something like:

import asyncio
import logging
import twitchio
from twitchio.ext import commands
from twitchio import eventsub

CLIENT_ID = "..."
CLIENT_SECRET = "..."
BOT_ID = "..."      # Your bot's user ID
OWNER_ID = "..."    # Your channel's user ID

class Bot(commands.Bot):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__(
            client_id=CLIENT_ID,
            client_secret=CLIENT_SECRET,
            bot_id=BOT_ID,
            owner_id=OWNER_ID,
            prefix="!"
        )

    async def setup_hook(self):
        # Subscribe to chat messages via EventSub
        sub = eventsub.ChatMessageSubscription(
            broadcaster_user_id=OWNER_ID,
            user_id=BOT_ID
        )
        await self.subscribe_websocket(payload=sub)

    async def event_ready(self):
        print(f"Bot is ready!")

    async def event_message(self, message: twitchio.ChatMessage):
        print(f"{message.chatter.name}: {message.text}")

async def main():
    twitchio.utils.setup_logging(level=logging.INFO)
    async with Bot() as bot:
        await bot.start()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())

Then:

  1. Run the bot

  2. log in as the Bot Account and visit http://localhost:4343/oauth?scopes=user:read:chat user:write:chat user:bot&force_verify=true

  3. Use you main account to visit http://localhost:4343/oauth?scopes=channel:bot&force_verify=true

After closing, check that tokens are saved to .tio.tokens.json and loaded on next start.

Refrenced: twitchio docs, twitchio quickstart guide

Q: How important is it to indicate if a class implements an interface in Perl? A:

I think you should upgrade to Moose if you are asking these questions. There you'll be able to define your interface by creating a role or class with appropriate abstract methods.

I agree with you that doing this can add valuable information. In Java there is the concept of a "marker interface," which is an empty interface which has no methods which exists only to tag a set of classes as being useful for a certain purpose. The most common example of this is the Serializable interface.

Of course, just because it can be useful does not mean it will be in your particular situation. :)
